subject: shiny-server cannot find the non-standard R library

messages.author: 5af4b8ae1d93bb56
messages.subject: shiny-server cannot find the non-standard R library
parts:
Hi All,

Today I installed a new Linux system with shiny-server for the testing purpose.
All examples from shiny packages are working great and look so neat.
As you know, all additional R packages are installed at /usr/lib64/R/library and automatically loaded at startup.
But if there's another library path, how can I configure the path so that the shiny-server recognizes all packages?

For example, I tried to load the ORE package which is installed at /u01/app/oracle/product/12.1.0/dbhome_1/R/library and
got the error message as attached. It says that shiny-server can not find or load the ORE package properly. So I believe
that shiny-server's configuration must be corrected in order to include the another library path.

Any idea about how to achieve this?

Thanks and Regards,
Sean

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: shiny-server cannot find the non-standard R library
parts:
Hi Sean,

I think the issue is which user has these libraries installed. If you open R and run `.libPaths()`, you'll be able to see which paths are included in your library search paths. These will likely be different for different users.

Now the question is which set of .libPaths is shiny-server using, and that will depend on how you have it configured. If you're using the autouser configuration, then each user's library will be used, because the applications will be run as that user. If you're using site_dir or app_dir, then the `run_as` setting will dictate which user runs Shiny (thus which .libPaths will be used).

My guess is that the `run_as` user you're using doesn't have these libraries installed. If that's the case, log in as that user, open R, and install the libraries.

Jeff
